_comment: SHARED golden vectors for the planetary hour: which planet rules a moment at a place. Read by BOTH runtimes:
Python     backend/tests/test_planetary_hours_golden.py (planetary_hour_at reproduces every vector)
backend/tests/test_planetary_hour_golden_vectors.py (the file against the classical table, no engine)
TypeScript src/lib/__tests__/planetaryHourGoldenVectors.test.ts
This file is the contract. There is one planetary-hour engine per runtime (backend/utils/planetary_hours.py and
src/lib/PlanetaryHourCalculator.ts) and the only thing that keeps them from drifting apart is that both must
reproduce every vector below.
BASIS of every value. The rulers, the hour numbers and the day rulers come from the Python reference,
planetary_hour_at (PR #996, merged as 61de751d; planetary_hours.py is as in its commit 6961ee36): the Sun's
events from the Swiss Ephemeris (pyswisseph 2.10.3.2, Moshier, as on Railway) at the standard depression of
0.8333 degrees, the weekday of the local mean solar date of the sunrise that began the planetary day (UTC +
longitude / 15 hours), the classical Chaldean sequence from the planet of that weekday. The reference was asked
at every stored instant (not only at the hour it was derived from). They do NOT come from the TypeScript code
under test, and the tests that read this file re-derive each ruler from the classical table, written out in the
test, without calling either engine.
Each record is one planetary day, from one sunrise to the next: the sunrise, the sunset and the next sunrise the
reference found (rounded to the second), the local mean solar date of that sunrise and its weekday, the planet of
that weekday, and the middle of each of the 24 hours: index 0-11 are the day hours from sunrise, 12-23 the night
hours from sunset, each [instant UTC, ruling planet]. A night hour whose instant is past local midnight belongs
to the planetary day that began the evening before: that is the case the old TypeScript code got wrong.
Regenerate with scripts/gen_planetary_hour_golden_vectors.py (needs backend/utils/planetary_hours.py). Do not edit by hand.

basis.reference: backend/utils/planetary_hours.py planetary_hour_at, PR #996 (merged 61de751d; the file as in 6961ee36)
basis.ephemeris: Swiss Ephemeris via pyswisseph 2.10.3.2, Moshier (no sweph_ephe/ files, as in the Railway image)
basis.weekday: local mean solar date of the sunrise that began the planetary day: UTC + longitude / 15 hours
basis.instants: the middle of each of the 24 planetary hours of the day, to the second
